seed: Most icons are built rather than drawn: a circle with a smaller circle cut out of it is a ring. This walk draws two overlapping circles, cuts the top one out of the one below from the layer row's own menu, and checks that what comes back is ONE path of TWO loops with a real hole in it, that its points can still be picked up and dragged, that the pill under the canvas says which shape's look survived, that one undo puts both circles back, and that Keep Overlap on two shapes that do not touch refuses out loud instead of emptying the canvas.

steps.note: a big circle with a smaller one sitting inside it, two separate rows in the layers list. Nothing about this is a ring yet: it is a disc with a disc on top of it
the row menu over two picked shapes offers 'Combine Shapes', where every other command about a layer already lives. Inside it are the four: Join, Cut Out, Keep Overlap, Drop Overlap

THE POINT: one layer, one path, made of TWO loops — the rim and the hole — with eight points on it and every run still a curve, not one of them flattened into a line. Compare doc-1-two-circles with doc-3-a-ring: the middle has gone transparent

the pill under the canvas names the shape whose fill, outline and effects the ring is wearing, and says it has a hole in it. Neither of those is on the canvas to be seen: two circles of the same colour say nothing about which was underneath
the rightmost point of the rim was picked up and pulled out, and the curves either side came with it. The hole is untouched: this is a shape, not a picture of one
one undo puts the dragged point back, the second takes the whole cut back to two circles: combining two shapes is ONE step, not two. Compare doc-6-both-back with doc-1-two-circles

THE OTHER HALF OF THE PROMISE: a circle away on its own, picked with the big one, asked for the overlap. There is none, so nothing is changed and the pill says why. The easy wrong answer here is to delete both shapes and leave a blank canvas
